# Open Festival Hub

Multi-festival, offline-first companion app. Two codebases (Next.js web + Jetpack Compose Android) sharing one JSON data source. No backend, no accounts, no tracking.

## What it is
White-label engine powering 6 festival apps (Sziget, Nova Rock, Frequency, Area 53, Ernte Punk, Rock am Ring — all 2026) from a single codebase. Config-first: all branding, colors, dates, and feature flags live in `festivals/<id>/config.json`.

## Platforms
- **Web**: Next.js 16 / React 19 static export (repo root) → GitHub Pages at https://atzsta13.github.io/studio/
- **Android**: single APK, Jetpack Compose / Kotlin 2.3 — `android/` directory

## Key constraints
- No API routes — fully static export; any `route.ts` breaks the build
- No camera features, no accounts, no social, no cloud AI (hard mandates)
- Offline-first: every core feature works with no signal
- No hardcoded colors, names, or coordinates in components
- `startTime`/`endTime` are ISO 8601 with offset; null for festivals without published schedules (Frequency, Ernte Punk)

## Canonical docs
- `AGENTS.md` — coding rules, architecture patterns, commands (start here)
- `TASKS.md` — open/unfinished work
- `docs/STATUS.md` — live state snapshot
- `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` — deep technical reference
- `docs/GOALS.md` — purpose of every feature
- `docs/features/FEATURES.md` — build status per feature per platform
- `docs/guides/MANDATES.md` — hard constraints
- `android/README.md` — Android file tree, Room schema, design system

## Data
Source of truth: `festivals/<id>/data/*.json`. Sync to apps: `npm run lineup:sync`.

## Verify before committing
```
npm run typecheck   # must return 0 errors
npm run lint        # must be clean
npm test -- --run   # 189 tests must pass
```
